traceability.evidence:
1) Specification under assessment - Story: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md - Core requirement: migrate from @story/@req to the new @supports annotation, with autofix, warnings, and documentation all targeting @supports. Examples and acceptance criteria explicitly show @supports (e.g. `@supports prompts/002.0-DEV-FETCH-AVAILABLE-VERSIONS.md REQ-AGE-CALC`).
2) Actual implemented rule and target format - Implementation file: src/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.ts - JSDoc header: - `ESLint rule implementation for preferring the consolidated @implements annotation over legacy combinations of @story and @req` - `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md` - Behavior: - Detects @story + @req comments and recommends migrating to @implements, not @supports. - Auto-fix builds `@implements ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}` (see applyImplementsReplacement): ```ts const implAnnotation = `@implements ${storyPath} ${reqIds.join(" ")}`; ... const implementsLine = `${linePrefix}${implAnnotation}`; ``` - No code anywhere in this rule constructs or emits @supports. - Messages (meta.messages): - preferImplements: "Consider using @implements instead of @story + @req for clearer traceability. Run ESLint with --fix to auto-convert." - cannotAutoFix: "Cannot auto-fix: {{reason}}. Manual migration to @implements required." - multiStoryDetected: "Multiple @story annotations detected in the same comment block. Manually convert to separate @implements lines." - The rule is opt‑in (type: "suggestion", docs.recommended: false, fixable: "code"). Configurability is by standard ESLint severities (off/warn/error), not by custom options.
3) Tests tied to the wrong story and to @implements, not @supports - Test file: tests/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.test.ts - Header: ```ts /** * Tests for: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md * @story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md */ ``` - All descriptions use MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS, not MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS: - `describe("prefer-implements-annotation rule (Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS)", ...)` - Key invalid tests assert migration to @implements: - Single @story + @req: ```ts code: `/**
 * @story ...
 * @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED
 */
function legacy() {}`, output: `/**
 * @implements ... REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED
 */
function legacy() {}`, errors: [{ messageId: "preferImplements" }], ``` - Multiple @req lines: ```ts output: `/**
 * @implements ... REQ-ONE REQ-TWO REQ-THREE
 */
function autoFixMultiReq() {}`, ``` - No tests mention @supports or expect @supports in outputs.
4) No @supports-based migration implemented in code or tests - A search for "supports" in source/tests showed no rule or logic targeting @supports: - `find_files` for "*supports*" in src/ and tests/ returned 0 files. - The only references to @supports are in the new story doc and ADR text, not in executable code.
5) Documentation for the rule still describes @implements, not @supports - docs/rules/prefer-implements-annotation.md: - Title: "Optional migration rule that recommends converting legacy @story + @req annotations to the newer @implements format." - Story tag: `@story docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md` - Examples: - Before: @story + @req - After (auto-fix): `@implements docs/stories/002.0-DEV-FETCH-AVAILABLE-VERSIONS.story.md REQ-AGE-CALC` - All narrative and examples are about @implements, not @supports. - docs/stories/developer-story.map.md still lists this story as "010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS".
6) Existence of the new @supports story vs. missing old story - Story under assessment: docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md (exists and clearly specifies @supports as the new target format). - There is NO corresponding docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS.story.md file anymore (grep and the .voder traceability XML confirm it is missing), yet all code and tests still reference that older path in @story tags.
7) Tests pass, but they validate @implements behavior, not this story’s @supports requirements - `npm test -- --verbose` shows the suite "prefer-implements-annotation rule (Story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS)" passing, with tests such as: - "[REQ-AUTO-FIX] single @story + single @req auto-fixes to single @implements line" - "[REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX] single @story with multiple @req lines auto-fixes to single @implements line containing all REQ IDs" - There are **no tests** that: - Expect an @supports line to be produced. - Validate that @supports passes any story/requirement validation rules. - Use the MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS story file in their @story annotations.
8) ADR status - docs/decisions/011-rename-implements-to-supports-annotation.accepted.md exists and describes a decision to rename @implements to @supports. - However, the actual rule implementation, tests, and docs have not been updated to use @supports; they remain on @implements.
Summary of acceptance criteria vs implementation: - Optional Warning (configurable, default off): Implemented (via ESLint severity) but specifically for recommending @implements, not @supports. - Auto-fix Support: Present, but converts @story + @req → @implements, not → @supports as required. - Single Story Conversion: Implemented for a single @story + multiple @req → one @implements line, not a @supports line. - Multi-story Detection: Implemented (mixed legacy/@implements and multiple @story paths), but messages and behavior are framed around @implements. - Preserve Order: Implemented for @implements insertion while preserving JSDoc structure. - Configurable Enforcement: Implemented via rule severity; tests verify the rule is disabled by default and can be "warn"/"error". - Both Formats Valid: Legacy @story/@req remain valid when the rule is off; tests cover this. - Quality Standards / Valid Output: Auto-fix output is valid @implements and passes existing @implements validation; **no implementation or validation for @supports output exists**. - Documentation: Migration docs and rule docs are written for @implements, not @supports, and all traceability annotations point to a now-missing MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS story.
Therefore, key story-specific requirements – especially that the migration and autofix target @supports and that the output passes @supports validation – are not implemented.
traceability.notes: FAILED because the implementation, tests, and documentation still implement migration from @story/@req to @implements via the prefer-implements-annotation rule, while this story explicitly requires migration to the new @supports format. Auto-fix output, rule messages, examples, and traceability annotations all reference @implements and a non-existent 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-IMPLEMENTS story file. No code or tests produce or validate @supports annotations. Configurability and backward-compatibility aspects are present, but the core functional requirement—to migrate to @supports—is not met for docs/stories/010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS.story.md.
